items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Dave Tuff decided he couldn't bear it any longer... so he got an offer to go to another place to play with some band from the University of Chicago and he took it... when the man heard me play, he wanted to kill me. He was so furious, but he was frightened that Dave Tuff would leave. So he threatene

ctx.x: No, don't let me get you ahead, go right back.

All right. I would like to go into this thing, because now we're, as I say, in Sheboygan, Wisconsin, and I am getting about $40 a week and that was a tremendous amount of money in those days-- that must have been what, 1924 or something, and of course, I was living at home and Dad never took any rent from us, from -- when I say us, I mean my brother, who has become a well-known actor, and we could always go home, you know, when we weren't doing anything. Well, at any rate, the music was so bad, really, because of…

started to rehearse a band and they said well -- the fellows in the band said, look, you are going to have to get a tenor, because C-Melody just isn't going to work and so about six months after that time -- and again, it's difficult for me to remember the year, Helen, but I should have thought it was about 1924, I got a tenor and now I was really confused because the few things that I had learned to play were now in another key. C-Melody being in C and the tenor being in B-flat.
